Read the passage below, based on the poem 'A Roadside Stand', and answer.

"At the bend in the highway, an old man and his granddaughter sit beside a table of cucumbers and a hand-painted sign: FRESH TODAY. Cars hiss past. Once, one slows, and the girl stands up, smoothing her dress. The driver only leans out to ask the way to the hill resort, then speeds off before she can answer."

"The scheme was announced with posters and speeches. The fishing families would be moved to new flats beside the highway, with a shopping centre and a cinema nearby. (iv) The tone of the passage is …  (a) ironic and critical  (b) comic  (c) neutral  (d) celebratory
items.answer: (i) To new flats beside the highway. (ii) (b) Boats rotted on the beach and the men had nothing to do (iii) (d) Resettling the poor near theatre and store makes them idle and dependent (iv) (a) ironic and critical
